accepted.s: According to the World Food Summit, 1996, food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to which of the following?
o: Food of their choice irrespective of dietary needs
Adequate food supplied exclusively by the government
Sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Food grains available only during periods of shortage
accepted.x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life.
accepted.tq: Use the precise official definition and reject the look-alike phrase ‘food of their choice’.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognized dimension of food security?
accepted.x: Availability, accessibility, affordability or access, utilisation/absorption and stability are associated with food security. Accountability is not a dimension.
accepted.tq: Find the odd term among the established dimensions.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s: Which of the following best distinguishes national food security from household food security?
o: National food security concerns only imports, whereas household food security concerns only domestic production.
National food security concerns aggregate availability, whereas household food security concerns actual access and affordability for each household.
National food security applies to urban areas, whereas household food security applies only to rural areas.
National food security is based on nutrition, whereas household food security is based only on buffer stocks.
accepted.x: National food security refers to adequate aggregate production and stocks. Household food security requires that each household can actually obtain and afford food.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into aggregate availability versus household-level access.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Food security remains necessary even in years of food surplus.
Reason (R): Starvation may result from unequal distribution even when aggregate food availability is adequate.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and unequal distribution explains why aggregate surplus does not automatically ensure household food security.
accepted.tq: Test whether the reason explains the distinction between national and household security.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s:
With reference to buffer stocks in India, consider the following statements:
1. Wheat and rice are procured by the Food Corporation of India from surplus states.
2. Procurement is made at a pre-announced Minimum Support Price on the advice of the CACP.
3. The procured grains may be sold at a lower issue price in deficit areas and during calamities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: FCI procures wheat and rice at the pre-announced MSP advised by CACP, and the stocks are released at lower issue prices in deficit areas or during calamities.
accepted.tq: Verify the agency, procurement price and purpose separately.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s: The strategic reserve of food grains is maintained at approximately what level above operational stocks?
accepted.x: The strategic reserve is maintained at 5 million tonnes above operational stocks.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific quantitative figure; the options are arranged in ascending order.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s: The principal purpose of OMSS (Domestic) sales of food grains is to:
o: Increase the procurement price paid to farmers
accepted.x: Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) sales are used to release food grains and help cool prices.
accepted.tq: Link the policy instrument with its stated market-stabilisation purpose.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s: The Bengal Famine of 1943 resulted in the death of approximately how many people?
accepted.x: The Bengal Famine of 1943 is stated to have caused approximately 30 lakh deaths.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the historically significant figure from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s:
Which of the following groups are identified among the most food-insecure sections of the population?
1. Scheduled Castes
2. Scheduled Tribes
3. Landless and poor OBC sections
4. Large landowning households
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and landless or poor OBC sections are identified as among the most food-insecure groups. Large landowning households are not included in this description.
accepted.tq: Identify the socially vulnerable groups and reject the reversed socio-economic category.
accepted.sec: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in the Public Distribution System in chronological order:
A. Targeted Public Distribution System
B. Revamped Public Distribution System
C. National Food Security Act
D. Initial Public Distribution System
Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The sequence is initial PDS in the 1940s, RPDS in June 1992, TPDS in June 1997 and NFSA in 2013.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest PDS stage first and then place the dated reforms.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: The Public Distribution System in India originated primarily as:
o: A World War II rationing measure
A replacement for the Integrated Child Development Services
accepted.x: The PDS began as a rationing measure during the Second World War, against the background of the Bengal famine.
accepted.tq: Use the historical origin rather than the later institutional form of the programme.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: The Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS) was introduced in June 1992 and covered approximately:
accepted.x: RPDS was introduced in June 1992 and covered 1,775 blocks.
accepted.tq: Match the reform year with its distinctive coverage figure.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Targeted Public Distribution System introduced in June 1997?
o: It classified beneficiaries into BPL and APL categories.
It provided only cooked meals through schools.
It replaced all nutrition services at anganwadis.
It supplied grain exclusively to export-oriented farmers.
accepted.x: TPDS was introduced in June 1997 with separate Below Poverty Line and Above Poverty Line categories.
accepted.tq: Use the programme's beneficiary classification as the identifying feature.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. PDS
b. ICDS
c. Mid-Day Meal/PM POSHAN
d. Food-for-Work

List-II (Food support)
i. Grain as wages
ii. Supplementary nutrition at anganwadis
iii. Subsidised or free grain through Fair Price Shops
iv. Hot cooked meal to eligible school-age children

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: PDS provides grain through Fair Price Shops; ICDS gives supplementary nutrition at anganwadis; PM POSHAN gives hot cooked meals; Food-for-Work gives grain as wages.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair ‘Food-for-Work—grain as wages’ and eliminate the codes.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) was initiated in 1975 on an:
accepted.x: ICDS began in 1975 as an experimental programme.
accepted.tq: Recall the programme's launch character, not merely its year.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Supplementary nutrition under ICDS is primarily provided through anganwadis to:
o: Only children aged 6–14 years enrolled in secondary schools
Children aged 0–6 years and pregnant and lactating women
accepted.x: ICDS provides supplementary nutrition through anganwadis to children aged 0–6 years and pregnant and lactating women.
accepted.tq: Match the service with its precise beneficiary groups.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Food-for-Work was introduced in India during:
accepted.x: The Food-for-Work programme was introduced in 1977–78 and provided grain as wages.
accepted.tq: Recall the programme year from the closely spaced historical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: The Mid-Day Meal/PM POSHAN programme is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
accepted.x: Mid-Day Meal, now PM POSHAN, is associated with the Ministry of Education.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry performs this function?’ authority test.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Under the present description of PM POSHAN, hot cooked meals are provided to:
o: Pregnant women and lactating mothers only
Bal Vatika/pre-school, primary and upper primary students
Only children in upper primary classes
Children below six months through anganwadis
accepted.x: PM POSHAN provides hot cooked meals to Bal Vatika or pre-school children and students at the primary and upper primary levels.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the school-meal beneficiary range from ICDS beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: TPDS was introduced in June 1997, not 1985. ICDS began in 1975, Mid-Day Meal in 1995, and Food-for-Work in 1977–78.
accepted.tq: Check each programme against its launch year and identify the swapped date.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Under the NFSA, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to:
o: Only subsidised wheat through Fair Price Shops
A monthly cash transfer of exactly ₹10,000 without food support
A take-home ration only after the child reaches six years
A free meal and a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000
accepted.x: NFSA provides pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal along with a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.
accepted.tq: Test the entitlement package as a combination of food support and maternity benefit.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Children in the age group of 6 months to 6 years are entitled under the NFSA to:
o: A take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS/anganwadi services
Only a school meal under PM POSHAN
accepted.x: Children aged 6 months to 6 years receive a take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS and anganwadi services.
accepted.tq: Separate the NFSA entitlement by age group and delivery channel.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Children between 6 and 14 years are covered under the NFSA food entitlement primarily through:
accepted.x: Children aged 6–14 years are entitled to a mid-day meal in school; the programme is now known as PM POSHAN.
accepted.tq: Match the age bracket with the appropriate institutional delivery mechanism.
accepted.sec: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

accepted.s: Who is most closely associated with the entitlement approach to understanding famine?
accepted.x: Amartya Sen developed the entitlement approach, especially in his work Poverty and Famines (1981).
accepted.tq: Identify the scholar associated with the named analytical approach.
accepted.sec: Entitlement approach - proponent

accepted.s: According to Amartya Sen's entitlement approach, famines primarily arise from:
o: A fall in aggregate food production in every case
An increase in the nutritional content of food
Excessive buffer stocks maintained by the government
A collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers
accepted.x: Sen argued that famine results from a collapse of people's entitlements or command over food, not merely from a decline in overall food availability.
accepted.tq: Reject the supply-only explanation and apply the income-and-entitlement concept.
accepted.sec: Entitlement approach - proponent

accepted.s: Poverty and Famines, which set out the entitlement approach to famine, was published in:
accepted.x: Amartya Sen's Poverty and Famines was published in 1981.
accepted.tq: Recall the associated publication year from the standard chronological options.
accepted.sec: Entitlement approach - proponent

accepted.s: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) was launched in 2020 primarily in the context of the:
o: National Food Security Act's original enactment in 2013
accepted.x: PMGKAY was launched in 2020 as part of the COVID-19 response and the Atmanirbhar package.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme with its crisis context rather than with the later NFSA merger.
accepted.sec: PMGKAY - launch, extensions, merger with NFSA

accepted.s: At its launch, PMGKAY provided what additional food-grain entitlement?
o: 10 kg of free grain per family irrespective of family size
5 kg of subsidised grain per household instead of NFSA benefits
One hot cooked meal per person per day through schools
5 kg of free grain per person over and above the NFSA entitlement
accepted.x: PMGKAY initially provided 5 kg of free food grains per person in addition to the existing NFSA entitlement.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an additional per-person entitlement from a household entitlement.
accepted.sec: PMGKAY - launch, extensions, merger with NFSA

accepted.s: From 1 January 2023, PMGKAY was subsumed with the NFSA entitlement. What was the principal effect of this decision?
o: The entitlement was converted into a cash transfer
NFSA allocations were discontinued for all beneficiaries
The entire NFSA allocation became free of cost
Only the APL category received free grain
accepted.x: From 1 January 2023, the entire NFSA allocation became free under the merged arrangement described as ‘One Nation–One Price–One Ration’.
accepted.tq: Test the policy change after merger rather than the original launch feature.
accepted.sec: PMGKAY - launch, extensions, merger with NFSA

accepted.s: For which period was the free food-grain arrangement under the extended PMGKAY continued?
accepted.x: The arrangement was extended for five years from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028.
accepted.tq: Use both boundary dates to distinguish the five-year extension.
accepted.sec: PMGKAY - launch, extensions, merger with NFSA

accepted.s: The approximate cost of the five-year extension of the free food-grain arrangement under PMGKAY is:
accepted.x: The cost of the five-year extension is approximately ₹11.80 lakh crore, borne by the Union Government.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive budgetary magnitude and reject nearby figures.
accepted.sec: PMGKAY - launch, extensions, merger with NFSA

accepted.s: The food subsidy provided in the Union Budget 2026–27 was:
accepted.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 provided ₹2,27,629 crore as food subsidy.
